newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Dutch seek talks with French left on EU treaty.
newsitem.headline: Dutch seek talks with French left on EU treaty.

text.p: The Netherlands unveiled the latest draft of a new European Union treaty on Monday and said it wanted talks as soon as possible with the new French Socialist government.

Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo said discussions with new Prime Minister Lionel Jospin could take place on June 10. The Netherlands holds the EU presidency until June 30, when Luxembourg takes over.
Van Mierlo said that despite the anti-EU tone of some campaign speeches he had no reason to believe that the treaty could not be completed at the June 16 and 17 summit.
"The elections cannot change anything in our timetable," he said. "We don't see any reason to make any change to any dot or comma because of the change of government in France."
Judging by the draft, the new treaty, which is designed to allow the bloc to enlarge into eastern Europe, is close to completion.

It calls for the EU to be turned into a freedom and security zone for its citizens, to place more emphasis on employment and the environment, to have a more efficient foreign policy and to take decisions in a more streamlined fashion.
Issues still to be decided include the size of the European Commission and the relative voting weights of different EU countries when they decide legisation.

Britain indicated again on Monday that it would not accept majority voting in foreign policy decisions. German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said Denmark, Greece and Ireland were also against losing the veto in that area.

Following elections in Britain and France, momentum is also clearly behind the adoption of an "Employment Chapter" in the new EU treaty, to force EU institutions to consider the effect in jobs of any decisions they take.
British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook described it as a "modest" proposal.
Germany remains the only country opposed, but is considered unlikely to block the move as long as it does not set numerical or other targets.
